items.headline: Record US EV sales in Q3 2025 before tax credit expiry
items.driver: Sales inflated by a rush to claim the $7,500 federal EV tax credit before it expired at the end of September 2025.
items.customer_relevance: Demand was partly incentive-driven; mass EV buyers are price-sensitive, premium buyers less so.
items.quote: Americans bought over 438,000 electric vehicles (EVs) in the third quarter of 2025 – a record number.
items.notes: Electrive (2025-10-13) gives 438,487 units for Q3 2025; share 10.5% per Cox (Cox later cites 10.6% as the Q3 record).

items.headline: US EV share fell to 5.8% after tax credit ended
items.driver: Congress and the president ended the $7,500 EV tax credit in September 2025; Q3 pull-forward then a Q4 drop.
items.customer_relevance: Without subsidy, EV demand in the US rests on product appeal; premium EV buyers must be won on merit.
items.quote: they crested 10% of the market in the third quarter before falling to just 5.8% in the fourth.
items.notes: Secondary reporting (InsideEVs) puts Q4 2025 at ~234,000 units, -46% QoQ, -36% YoY; not fetched (502). Cox's Stephanie Valdez Streaty reportedly said premium buyers are far less dependent on the credit (unverified).

items.headline: US EV share 7.8% in 2025, nearly flat versus 2024
items.driver: Q3 rush before credit expiry offset the Q4 slump, leaving full-year share near 2024's 8.1%.
items.customer_relevance: US EV adoption plateaued; ICE/PHEV/hybrid options remain essential for US premium buyers through successor launch.
items.quote: EVs made up 7.8% of the new cars Americans bought in 2025, nearly matching the 8.1% of 2024.

items.headline: US EV sales down 20.5% YoY in Q2 2026, up QoQ
items.driver: Third straight quarter of sharp YoY declines after incentives expired; elevated gas prices and state incentives supported a 14.7% QoQ rebound.
items.customer_relevance: Fuel-price spikes revive interest in efficient drivetrains; EVs in the US now compete without federal subsidy.
items.quote: 247,226 EVs were sold in the second quarter
items.notes: Cox: EV share ~5.8% of new-vehicle volume in Q2 2026, roughly unchanged from Q1, vs record 10.6% in Q3 2025. Secondary reports: H1 2026 YTD 462,892, -23.8% (not verified on Cox page). Cox text: 'Elevated gas prices continue to support demand for fuel-efficient vehicles'.

items.headline: US EV share stuck near 5.8% in Q2 2026
items.driver: Post-credit demand reset; share roughly unchanged from Q1 2026 and well below Q3 2025 record.
items.customer_relevance: US EV share is stable but low; successor plans for the US need strong ICE/PHEV variants.
items.quote: EVs were about 5.8% of new-vehicle volume in Q2
items.notes: Quote is a close paraphrase returned by the fetch tool, not confirmed verbatim.

items.headline: US proposes CAFE rollback to about 34.5 mpg by MY2031
items.driver: Administration says the rollback would cut about $1,000 off the average new-vehicle price; replaces the ~50 mpg Biden-era target.
items.customer_relevance: Less regulatory push toward efficiency in US; buyer demand for large ICE/PHEV premium cars may persist longer.
items.quote: setting the industry average for light-duty vehicles at roughly 34.5 miles per gallon through the 2031 model year
items.notes: Unit is mpg (schema has no mpg unit; 'points' used). NHTSA's own savings estimate reported elsewhere as ~$900-930/vehicle; CBS says Biden-era rule was 50 mpg (others say 50.4). Proposal announced 2025-12-03; not final at checkpoint.

items.headline: EPA repeals endangerment finding, ending federal vehicle GHG standards
items.driver: EPA concluded it lacks statutory authority under section 202(a) to regulate vehicle emissions for climate change; states and NGOs announced legal challenges.
items.customer_relevance: Federal pressure to electrify US fleets removed; US buyer choice driven by price, fuel cost and product, not regulation.
items.quote: On February 12, 2026, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA") finalized the repeal of the 2009 Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding
items.notes: Page shows only 'February 2026'; published_at set to the event date. Harvard EELP tracker gives Feb 18. Rule 'eliminates all federal greenhouse gas emission standards for motor vehicles'. Litigation pending.

items.headline: US confirms 15% tariff on EU cars, retroactive to 1 Aug 2025
items.driver: US-EU framework deal (late July 2025) cut the auto tariff from 25%; formal notice issued in September 2025.
items.customer_relevance: German-built imports (e.g. 5/7 Series from Dingolfing) carry ~15% duty in US; pricing headroom for features shrinks.
items.quote: confirming that autos and auto parts imports will be subject to a 15% duty from August 1
items.notes: KBB (2025-07-28) reported the deal as 15% 'instead of the 25% levy they have faced since April'. A Car Dealership Guy piece claims 15% plus 2.5% levy; most sources treat 15% as all-inclusive.

items.headline: Trump threatens to raise EU car tariff back to 25%
items.driver: Trump said the EU 'is not complying' with the trade deal; US-built vehicles would be excluded.
items.customer_relevance: Renewed price risk for German-built premium imports in the US; US-built SUVs (Spartanburg) insulated.
items.quote: is not complying with our fully agreed to Trade Deal
items.notes: Euronews (2026-06-02) reports the threat was tied to EU implementation by 4 July 2026. Whether 25% was ever applied is not confirmed by any fetched source up to 2026-07-31.

items.headline: Higher EU car tariff would mostly hit luxury imports
items.driver: European brands build mid-range cars in US; finished imports are usually higher-end, e.g. S-Class, BMW 3 and 4 Series built in Germany.
items.customer_relevance: Executive/luxury sedans imported from Germany face the largest US price exposure versus US-built SUVs.
items.quote: The tariffs would mostly hit higher-end and luxury vehicles.
items.notes: Article cites ACEA: US takes 29% of EU car export value.

items.headline: European Parliament approves EU-US deal, defusing car tariff threat
items.driver: Plenary approval (440 for, 151 against, 50 abstentions) puts EU on track to implement deal before Trump's deadline.
items.customer_relevance: If implemented, US tariff on EU cars likely stays 15%; uncertainty for German-built premium imports eases.
items.quote: defuse his threat of new tariffs on European vehicles
items.notes: Value = votes in favour (unit 'points' as placeholder). Member-state sign-off and Official Journal publication still pending at article date. Sunset clause reported as March 2028 (Euronews) vs end-2029 (AFP).

items.headline: US cuts Korean car tariff to 15%, retroactive to 1 Nov
items.driver: US Commerce Department implemented the Korea trade deal after Korea submitted its investment bill.
items.customer_relevance: Hyundai/Kia/Genesis regain tariff parity with EU and Japan imports in the US premium-adjacent market.
items.quote: tariffs on South Korean automobiles would be retroactively reduced to 15% starting from November 1
items.notes: Korea Times (2025-11-11): EU paid 15% since Aug 1, Japan since Sep 16, 2025; Hyundai Q3 2025 operating profit -29%, Kia -49%, largely due to tariffs.

items.headline: Japanese cars pay 15% US tariff since 16 Sep 2025
items.driver: US-Japan trade agreement lowered the auto tariff from 25% to 15%.
items.customer_relevance: Lexus and other Japanese imports face similar US tariff burden as German-built BMWs.
items.quote: Japanese carmakers have paid it since September 16
items.notes: Quote is a paraphrase returned by the fetch tool; date consistent with widely reported 16 Sep 2025 implementation.

items.headline: Supreme Court strikes IEEPA tariffs; Section 232 car tariffs stay
items.driver: Court ruled 6-3 on 20 Feb 2026 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; Section 232 auto duties (25%, or 15% under deals) unaffected.
items.customer_relevance: No tariff relief for imported premium cars; US price levels for imports stay elevated.
items.quote: the Section 232 tariffs are still very much in force.
items.notes: Value = Section 232 base rate on passenger vehicles. Automotive Logistics (2026-02-23): new 10% Section 122 global surcharge exempts passenger vehicles and certain parts.

items.headline: BMW, Porsche, Audi raise US prices citing tariffs
items.driver: BMW ~1% ($400-1,500) for 2026 excl. EVs; Porsche +1.2-2.9% from Jan 2026; Audi +$800-4,100; Mercedes largely absorbed costs.
items.customer_relevance: US premium buyers face higher sticker prices; value-for-money of standard equipment gains weight.
items.quote: 15% tariff on every exported vehicle will result in billions of dollars in additional costs
items.notes: Quote is a shortened VDA statement as returned by fetch tool. VW expected up to EUR 5bn tariff hit in 2025; Mercedes EUR 362m on adj. EBIT. German car exports reportedly -14% in first three quarters 2025.

items.headline: US average new-car price hits record $50,326 in December
items.driver: December seasonality and a mix skewed to luxury vehicles and full-size pickups; nearly 20% of buyers chose luxury.
items.customer_relevance: Affordability strain in mass market while affluent buyers keep spending; premium demand remains resilient.
items.quote: Kelley Blue Book says the average transaction price for a new vehicle climbed to $50,326 in the final month of 2025.
items.notes: Carscoops also: 'Nearly 20 percent of shoppers went for luxury rides in December'; incentives 7.5% of ATP; EV ATP just over $58,000. KBB ATP excludes incentives.

items.headline: US average new-car price $49,758 in June 2026
items.driver: Prices broadly flat YoY (+0.6%) despite tariffs; KBB ATP excludes incentives.
items.customer_relevance: Price growth has stalled; buyers are stretched by financing costs, limiting room for price-driven upgrades.
items.notes: Extracted from Cox PDF tables (June 2026 vs May 2026 vs June 2025).

items.headline: BMW brand US average transaction price $73,932 in December
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book make-level average; excludes incentives.
items.customer_relevance: BMW US pricing stable YoY despite tariffs; tariff costs partly absorbed.
items.notes: Make row (BMW brand). Manufacturer row BMW Group: $72,137, +1.1% YoY.

items.headline: BMW brand US average transaction price $73,514 in June
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book make-level average; excludes incentives. Modest YoY rise.
items.customer_relevance: BMW US prices stable; little evidence of large tariff pass-through to transaction prices.
items.notes: Make row. Manufacturer row BMW Group: $71,666, +1.3% YoY.

items.headline: Mercedes-Benz US average transaction price down 6.2% YoY
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book make-level average; excludes incentives.
items.customer_relevance: Competitor price pressure in US premium segment; buyers can get more car for the money.

items.headline: Mercedes-Benz US average transaction price down 3.9% YoY
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book make-level average; excludes incentives.
items.customer_relevance: Continued competitor price softness in US premium segment.

items.headline: US 'Luxury Car' segment average price $62,558, +6.2% YoY
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book segment average; excludes incentives. Segment definition is KBB's (sedans).
items.customer_relevance: Luxury sedan prices rising faster than market; buyers expect visible value for higher outlay.
items.notes: Mapping KBB 'Luxury Car' to executive segment is an assumption.

items.headline: US 'Luxury Car' segment average price $60,852, +5.1% YoY
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book segment average; excludes incentives.
items.customer_relevance: Luxury sedan price inflation continues into 2026.
items.notes: Mapping KBB 'Luxury Car' to executive segment is an assumption.

items.headline: US entry-level luxury car average price $57,649, +2.7% YoY
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book segment average; excludes incentives.
items.customer_relevance: Entry premium is getting pricier, raising the bar for perceived value.
items.notes: 1 Series (F70) is not sold in the US; context only.

items.headline: US entry-level luxury car average price $61,271, +6.9% YoY
items.driver: Kelley Blue Book segment average; excludes incentives.
items.customer_relevance: Entry premium price inflation accelerated in H1 2026.

items.headline: Fed cuts rates to 3.50-3.75%, third cut in a row
items.driver: FOMC cited softening labour market; third consecutive 25bp cut after September and October 2025.
items.customer_relevance: Slightly lower financing costs could support leasing/financing of premium cars in 2026.
items.quote: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point
items.notes: Value is the midpoint of 3.50-3.75%.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% as energy shock lifts inflation
items.driver: Inflation elevated partly from supply shocks raising energy prices; no cuts since December 2025.
items.customer_relevance: No financing relief for car buyers in 2026; monthly payment affordability stays a key purchase barrier.
items.quote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent
items.notes: Statement also: 'Inflation remains elevated ... in part reflecting supply shocks ... that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy.' Secondary sources: June dot plot raised 2026 rate expectations (unverified).

items.headline: Record 20.3% of US new-car loans exceed $1,000 monthly
items.driver: Edmunds: high prices pushed amount financed to record $43,759 and average payment to $772; APR dipped to 6.7%.
items.customer_relevance: Affordability pressure even near premium; flexible packages, leasing and long-term value matter more.
items.quote: reached a record high of 20.3% of all financed new-vehicle purchases in Q4 2025
items.notes: Also: 'The average annual percentage rate (APR) for new-vehicle purchases dipped slightly to 6.7% in Q4 2025'.

items.headline: One in five US new-car buyers pay $1,000+ monthly
items.driver: Edmunds: APR ticked back up to 7.0%, record $777 average payment, record 23.9% on 84+ month loans.
items.customer_relevance: Financing burden rising; premium buyers may trade down trims or extend terms, valuing residual value.
items.quote: One in five (20.3%) new-vehicle financers in Q2 took on monthly payments of $1,000 or more
items.notes: Also: 'APRs, which ticked back up to 7.0% in Q2'.

items.headline: US consumer sentiment 52.9 in December, far below 2024
items.driver: Durable-goods buying conditions fell for a fifth month, tied to prices and financing conditions.
items.customer_relevance: Weak sentiment favours cautious purchases; value, warranty and running costs gain importance.
items.quote: The University of Michigan's Index of Consumer Sentiment rose to 52.9 in December 2025
items.notes: YoY -28.5% per Nasdaq/RTTNews summary (not fetched). Same page: 'Buying conditions for durable goods fell for a fifth consecutive month'.

items.headline: US sentiment 48.9 in June after record-low May
items.driver: Early-month easing in gasoline prices brought relief; May's 44.8 was a record low amid Iran-conflict energy shock.
items.customer_relevance: Fuel-cost anxiety and low confidence push buyers toward efficiency and cautious spending.
items.quote: The Index of Consumer Sentiment registered 48.9 in the preliminary June release
items.notes: Preliminary reading; final June reported at 49.5 by secondary sources (not verified). Iran-conflict link from Trading Economics (2026-07-17), which mentions a 'July 7 resumption of US strikes against Iran'.

items.headline: EIA expected US gasoline prices to fall 6% in 2026
items.driver: Lower crude oil prices forecast (Brent ~$56/b in 2026 per secondary summaries).
items.customer_relevance: Cheap fuel weakens running-cost argument for EVs/PHEVs among US buyers.
items.quote: we forecast retail U.S. gasoline prices will be lower the next two years than in 2025, falling 6% in 2026
items.notes: January 2026 STEO table reportedly $3.10/gal 2025 and $2.92/gal 2026 (secondary, not verified).

items.headline: EIA now sees 2026 US gasoline at $3.64 per gallon
items.driver: Crude price spike and tight gasoline supply in spring 2026; EIA expects ~41 cents/gal decline in Q3 as crude eases.
items.customer_relevance: Fuel cost became a salient purchase factor in 2026, boosting hybrids and efficient drivetrains.
items.quote: lower crude oil prices will contribute to retail gasoline prices falling by about 41 cents per gallon
items.notes: Forecast up from $2.92 (Jan STEO) to $3.90 (June STEO) then $3.64 (July STEO). EIA weekly retail: $3.777/gal on 2026-07-06. Secondary EIA monthly data: Feb 2026 $2.908, May 2026 $4.479 (not verified).

items.headline: China NEV purchase tax returns at 5%, relief capped 15,000 yuan
items.driver: 2023 MoF notice: NEVs bought 2026-2027 get 50% purchase-tax reduction, capped at 15,000 yuan per car.
items.customer_relevance: Premium NEVs above ~300k yuan lose more of the benefit; pull-forward into late 2025 depresses early 2026.
items.quote: NEVs purchased between January 1, 2026, and December 31, 2027
items.notes: Value = cap on tax reduction. Tighter technical requirements for PHEVs from 2026 reported (S&P, Benchmark) but not verified here.

items.headline: China car sales fell 20% in January after tax change
items.driver: NEV purchase tax reinstated at 5% on 1 Jan 2026 after year-end pull-forward; sharpest monthly decline in nearly two years.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese buyers are highly policy- and price-sensitive; demand timing follows incentive changes.
items.quote: Passenger car sales fell 20% year over year to 1.4 million units, the sharpest monthly decline in nearly two years.
items.notes: Page metadata says datePublished 2026-02-13. Not CPCA primary; check CPCA for exact January figure.

items.headline: China NEV retail record 1.337 million in December 2025
items.driver: Year-end deliveries accelerated so buyers could benefit from 2025 tax policy; growth momentum slowing.
items.customer_relevance: NEV is mainstream in China (54% share 2025); premium entrants must compete on tech and value.
items.quote: Passenger NEV retail sales reached 1.337 million units in December
items.notes: FY2025 NEV retail 12.81m (+17.6%), penetration 53.96%. Total PV retail Dec 2.261m (-14%). Preliminary (Jan 7) figure was 1.387m / 60.4% penetration.

items.headline: China NEV retail fell YoY for sixth straight month
items.driver: CPCA: high oil prices and shifting preferences accelerate electrification even as overall demand falls; penetration 62.8%.
items.customer_relevance: NEV share keeps rising while total market shrinks; ICE premium demand in China under strong pressure.
items.quote: China's new energy vehicle (NEV) retail sales fell year-on-year in June for the sixth consecutive month.
items.notes: Preliminary (Jul 3): 1.037m, -7%. Final penetration 62.8%.

items.headline: China passenger car retail down 20% in H1 2026
items.driver: Weak demand after purchase-tax change; June also hit by high base, weak 618 promotions, collapse in gasoline-car sales.
items.customer_relevance: Shrinking Chinese market intensifies competition; premium imports and JV brands lose volume.
items.quote: China's cumulative retail sales of passenger vehicles so far this year were 8,750,000 units
items.notes: Preliminary. Chinaevhome (2026-07-08) gives H1 8.701m, -20.2%. FY2025 total PV retail 23.744m, +3.8% (Gasgoo, not fetched).

items.headline: China gasoline-car retail plunged 39% YoY in June
items.driver: CPCA: high oil prices and shifting consumer preferences accelerate electrification.
items.customer_relevance: ICE-based premium models (e.g. 5 Series LWB ICE) face shrinking Chinese demand; electrified variants essential.
items.quote: high oil prices and shifting consumer preferences are accelerating the pace of electrification.
items.notes: Pure gasoline -42%, ordinary hybrids -7% (per same article).

items.headline: China 2026 trade-in subsidy becomes % of price, capped
items.driver: Scrappage: NEV 12% up to 20,000 yuan; ICE <=2.0L 10% up to 15,000. Trade-in: 8%/15,000 and 6%/13,000.
items.customer_relevance: Pricier cars hit caps, keeping full subsidy; ICE above 2.0L excluded, hurting larger-engine premium variants.
items.quote: shifts from fixed subsidies to a percentage-based model with maximum caps
items.notes: Issuer reported as NDRC/MoF (CarNewsChina) or MOFCOM and other departments (RTHK, Gasgoo). Effective 1 Jan 2026.

items.headline: 2026 trade-in subsidy implemented across many Chinese regions
items.driver: Local programmes launched on national rules; one subsidy per person; deadlines end-2026 to 10 Jan 2027.
items.customer_relevance: Subsidy remains available through 2026 but did not prevent a 20% H1 market decline.
items.quote: The 2026 vehicle trade-in subsidy policy has already been implemented in many regions across China
items.notes: No citable source found on 2026 funding pauses (searched; budget limit hit).

items.headline: China drafts rules banning below-cost car pricing
items.driver: SAMR draft 'Guidelines for Price Behavior Compliance in the Automotive Industry' targets price-war 'involution'.
items.customer_relevance: Fewer deep discounts may stabilise transaction prices, helping premium brands' price positioning in China.
items.quote: Improper pricing practices, including sales below cost, will be penalized.
items.notes: Draft for public comment.

items.headline: SAMR issues car pricing guidelines banning below-cost sales
items.driver: Anti-involution push against price war; issued 12 Feb 2026 amid sharp January sales fall.
items.customer_relevance: Price-war relief could restore value perception, but competition shifts to features and tech content.
items.quote: SAMR's new guidelines prohibit automakers from pricing below production cost to 'squeeze out competitors.'
items.notes: Other reports date issuance to 11 Feb 2026 (China Law & Practice listing). Official SAMR text not fetched.

items.headline: China lowers luxury car consumption-tax threshold to 900,000 yuan
items.driver: MoF/STA notice to 'guide reasonable consumption'; BEVs included for the first time; effective 20 Jul 2025.
items.customer_relevance: Top 7 Series/i7 trims in China above threshold get pricier; demand may shift to lower trims.
items.quote: The threshold for the luxury car consumption tax has been lowered to RMB 900,000 ($125,330) excluding VAT
items.notes: Previously RMB 1.3m. Rate 10% at retail per KPMG/Gasgoo (not verified on fetched page).

items.headline: China bans 'self-driving' marketing terms, tightens OTA rules
items.driver: MIIT measures after fatal Xiaomi SU7 crash; systems must be labelled by assisted-driving level; public beta tests ended.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese buyers still value ADAS, but claims must be precise; safety and validated features matter.
items.quote: over-the-air updates can only be transmitted after validation has been completed.
items.notes: Draft mandatory national standard for combined driving assistance opened Sept 2025 (secondary); 2026 finalization not verified.

items.headline: China NEV exports up 119.8% YoY in December 2025
items.driver: Export growth offsets slowing domestic demand.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese NEV brands expanding abroad; more competition for BMW in EU, Asia and Middle East.
items.quote: Passenger NEVs exported from China in December totaled 273,000 units, up 119.8% year-on-year.
items.notes: Quote returned by fetch tool in quotes but may be lightly paraphrased.

items.headline: China passenger car exports 877,000 in June, up 82%
items.driver: Exports became the market's main growth engine as domestic demand weakened; exports 37% of PV sales vs 19% a year earlier.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese brands push harder into BMW's export markets with feature-rich, keenly priced cars.
items.quote: Passenger vehicle exports, including complete vehicles and CKD kits, reached 877K units in June, up 82.3% year on year.
items.notes: CnEVPost: NEV exports 499,000 (+152.7%), 56.9% of PV exports.

items.headline: BMW China deliveries fell 20.4% in H1 2026
items.driver: Source names no specific cause; Q2 China down 30.2% amid weak Chinese market.
items.customer_relevance: Foreign premium brands losing ground in China; local tech expectations rise.
items.quote: Der Haken: In China bricht der Absatz im Halbjahr um 20,4% ein, im zweiten Quartal sogar um 30,2%.
items.notes: Search summaries give 261,773 units; confirm against BMW Group H1 release. Likely duplicated in OEM topic file.

items.headline: EU proposes 90% CO2 cut for 2035, not 100%
items.driver: Automotive package: remaining 10% offset via EU low-carbon steel, e-fuels and biofuels; PHEVs, range extenders can stay after 2035.
items.customer_relevance: Reduces pressure for BEV-only successors in EU; PHEV/EREV variants remain relevant to buyers beyond 2035.
items.quote: From 2035 onwards, carmakers will need to comply with a 90% tailpipe emissions reduction target
items.notes: Proposal only; needs Parliament and Council. Also 'banking & borrowing' for 2030-2032. The earlier 2025 amendment allowing 2025-2027 three-year averaging was not re-sourced here.

items.headline: EU proposes zero/low-emission quotas for large-company fleets from 2030
items.driver: Automotive package: Member-State-level targets for large companies, with a separate zero-emission sub-target.
items.customer_relevance: Company-car buyers (key for 5 Series in DE/UK) will increasingly need BEV/PHEV variants.
items.quote: From 2030 onwards, Member States must ensure that a minimum share of new corporate cars and vans registered by large companies are zero- or low-emission
items.notes: Percentages not on page; vary by Member State.

items.headline: EU plans super-credits for small affordable EVs up to 4.2 m
items.driver: Small Affordable Cars initiative creates a new vehicle category to boost affordable EV supply.
items.customer_relevance: Cheap small EVs get regulatory boost; premium compact (1 Series) must differentiate on quality, not price.
items.quote: car manufacturers will be able to benefit from "super credits" for small affordable electric cars
items.notes: Category covers EVs up to 4.2 m length (F70 1 Series is longer, assumption).

items.headline: EU and China agree guidance on minimum prices for Chinese EVs
items.driver: Price undertakings may replace EU countervailing duties of up to 35.3% on Chinese-made BEVs.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese EVs in Europe may get cheaper or more available, raising value pressure on premium BEVs.
items.quote: The EU will set a minimum import price for each Chinese NEV maker.
items.notes: Quote attributed to CCCME in article; fetch tool marked it as a quote but fidelity uncertain. Commission guidance issued 12 Jan 2026. No accepted undertakings verified by 2026-07-31 (gap).

items.headline: Germany revives income-based EV subsidy, EUR 3,000-6,000
items.driver: EUR 3bn from Climate and Transformation Fund for ~800,000 vehicles; households up to EUR 80,000-90,000 taxable income.
items.customer_relevance: Reopens private EV demand in Germany for mid-income buyers; PHEVs qualify only if <=60 g/km or >=80 km range.
items.quote: the incentive applies retroactively from 1 January 2026
items.notes: Base EUR 3,000 BEV, EUR 1,500 PHEV/EREV; max EUR 6,000. PHEV support limited to registrations until 30 June 2027. Applications expected Q2 2026 (newmobility). Portal opening/uptake not verified for 2026-07.

items.headline: German EV subsidy has no vehicle price cap
items.driver: Unlike earlier schemes, eligibility depends on household income, not list price; i7 or iX could theoretically qualify.
items.customer_relevance: Mid-income German buyers of premium EVs/PHEVs (iX1, i5, 530e) can get subsidy; affluent buyers excluded by income.
items.quote: A notable change from previous subsidy programs is the absence of a maximum purchase price limit.
items.notes: Based on BimmerToday report; not checked against official programme text.

items.headline: German 0.25% company-car tax for BEVs up to EUR 100,000
items.driver: Low benefit-in-kind rate for electric company cars, cap raised in 2025; valid through 2030.
items.customer_relevance: Makes BEV versions of 5 Series/i5 attractive for German company-car drivers.
items.quote: Employees using fully electric company cars with a list price ≤€100,000 (increased from €95,000 in 2025)
items.notes: Page says 'updated for 2025, published on 18th April 2025' but contains later rolling updates; prior cap commonly reported as EUR 70,000 (conflict). Page also lists 40% special depreciation for company BEVs.

items.headline: France funds EV bonus via energy-saving certificates (coup de pouce)
items.driver: State bonus replaced/supplemented by CEE-funded premium; social leasing reactivated for 2026.
items.customer_relevance: French incentives target low/middle incomes and cheaper cars; premium EVs largely excluded.
items.quote: offering approximately €3,000 for middle-income households and up to €5,700 for low-income households
items.notes: Region set to EU (schema has no FR). Page update date unclear; 2025 bonus required price < EUR 47,000 and environmental score. Verify with French official sources.

items.headline: Spain's MOVES III ended 2025; Plan Auto+ point-of-sale aid follows
items.driver: Successor scheme applies incentive as dealer discount; IRPF 15% EV deduction extended through 2026.
items.customer_relevance: Spanish incentives capped by price (MOVES III: BEV < EUR 45,000 excl. VAT); premium mostly excluded.
items.quote: The 'Plan MOVES III' concluded on 31 December 2025.
items.notes: Region set to EU (schema has no ES). Page update date unclear; Plan Auto+ amounts not given.

items.headline: Italy's EUR 597m EV bonus exhausted within 24 hours
items.driver: Up to EUR 11,000 with scrappage for ISEE up to EUR 30,000; 55,680 vouchers requested.
items.customer_relevance: Pent-up affordable EV demand in Italy when subsidised; little direct effect on premium segment.
items.quote: The fund was exhausted after just 24 hours.
items.notes: Region EU (schema has no IT). Budget given as ~EUR 600m, updated EUR 595m; others say EUR 597m.

items.headline: UK Electric Car Grant up to GBP 3,750, cars under GBP 37,000
items.driver: Grant launched July 2025; banded by sustainability; extended with extra GBP 1.3bn to 2029/30.
items.customer_relevance: Most BMW EVs exceed the GBP 37,000 cap; grant helps mass-market rivals, not premium.
items.quote: The grant value is £3,750 for the greenest EVs, or £1,500 for other qualifying models.
items.notes: Value in GBP (schema has no gbp unit).

items.headline: UK adds GBP 1.3bn to Electric Car Grant, runs to 2029-30
items.driver: Autumn Budget 2025 decision to support EV uptake under ZEV mandate.
items.customer_relevance: Sustained subsidy for cheaper EVs in UK through successor launch window.
items.quote: boosting the programme with an additional £1.3 billion of funding and extending it to run until 2029‑30
items.notes: Value in GBP.

items.headline: UK to charge EVs and PHEVs per mile from April 2028
items.driver: Budget 2025: eVED mileage charge, roughly half the fuel duty rate paid by average petrol/diesel driver.
items.customer_relevance: UK EV running-cost advantage narrows from 2028; efficiency and range per kWh gain relevance.
items.quote: a new mileage charge for electric and plug-in hybrid cars, which will come into effect from April 2028
items.notes: Widely reported rates 3p/mile BEV and 1.5p/mile PHEV not confirmed on the fetched portion of the page.

items.headline: UK raises EV Expensive Car Supplement threshold to GBP 50,000
items.driver: Budget 2025 eases VED surcharge for new EVs from 1 April 2026.
items.customer_relevance: More premium EVs (e.g. i4, entry i5) escape the surcharge; matters for UK premium EV pricing.
items.quote: increasing the threshold at which motorists with new EVs have to pay the VED Expensive Car Supplement from £40,000 to £50,000
items.notes: Value in GBP.

items.headline: Japan raises EV subsidy cap to 1.3 million yen from January
items.driver: METI revised CEV subsidy caps mid-period (announced 18 Dec 2025): EV 900k to 1.3m yen, PHEV 600k to 850k yen.
items.customer_relevance: Larger subsidies could lift EV/PHEV demand in Japan, relevant to F70's sizeable Japan customer base.
items.quote: 2025年12月18日、2024年12月から実施中のクリーンエネルギー自動車導入促進補助金（以下CEV補助金）について、補助上限額の見直しが経済産業省から発表された。
items.notes: Value in JPY. Article gives no trade-related rationale; secondary reports link change to US trade talks (unverified).

items.headline: Japan's new EV subsidy scoring cuts BYD aid, favours domestic supply
items.driver: From 1 April 2026, half of 200 points tied to supply-chain security and domestic production; Tesla keeps ~1.27m yen.
items.customer_relevance: Imported EV subsidies in Japan vary widely; supply-chain criteria decide premium EV price competitiveness.
items.quote: Japan will sharply reduce purchase subsidies for several electric vehicles sold by China's BYD
items.notes: Value = new subsidy for BYD Atto 3/Seal (JPY). Paywalled; scoring details from AI digest on page. BMW subsidy levels not found.
